title: CVE-2026-9545: exposing HTTP/3 early data
explain: The code supports the reported flaw. A maintainer should review its impact and decide what to do next.
summary: The report claims that curl's HTTP/3 early data implementation incorrectly sends request data before TLS handshake verification completes when reusing a session that supports early data, leading to potential disclosure of sensitive request material to an attacker controlling the server certificate.

claims.text: cf_ngtcp2_send() does not require successful peer verification before opening an HTTP/3 stream, buffering request bytes, or flushing egress
claims.reasoning: The code in cf_ngtcp2_send() only rejects sending if ctx->tls_vrfy_result is already set (a prior verification failure). It does not check ctx->tls_handshake_complete before opening streams, buffering request data, or flushing egress. Lines 1812-1813 explicitly acknowledge that data is written when the handshake is not complete and early data is enabled.

citations.note: Only checks ctx->tls_vrfy_result (pre-existing verification error), not ctx->tls_handshake_complete
Opens HTTP/3 stream via h3_stream_open() without requiring tls_handshake_complete

Explicitly tracks earlydata_skip when !ctx->tls_handshake_complete && ctx->use_earlydata, confirming data is sent before handshake completes
Calls cf_progress_egress() to flush egress without requiring successful peer verification

claims.text: in curl_ngtcp2.c function cf_ngtcp2_send() around lines 1732-1824
claims.reasoning: The function cf_ngtcp2_send is defined at lines 1732-1825 in lib/vquic/curl_ngtcp2.c, matching the report's location claim.

claims.text: reusing an ngtcp2 HTTP/3 session that advertises early data support after the server's certificate changes
claims.reasoning: cf_ngtcp2_on_session_reuse() initializes the HTTP/3 connection (init_ngh3_conn), sets use_earlydata=TRUE, and marks the filter as connected (cf->connected=TRUE) at lines 2581-2584, all before the new QUIC/TLS handshake completes. This enables the early data path in cf_ngtcp2_send().

claims.text: sensitive request material such as cookies, bearer tokens, or request body can be disclosed to an attacker
claims.reasoning: The PoC demonstrates that the Authorization header and request body are sent as early data (visible in server log) before certificate verification fails. The code path in cf_ngtcp2_send() processes headers via h3_stream_open() and writes request bytes to the send buffer, which are then flushed via cf_progress_egress() before handshake completion.

Early data including request bytes tracked in earlydata_skip before handshake completes

claims.text: perform a valid HTTP/3 request to cache an H3 TLS session, restart the server with a distinct ticket key and evil.example.com certificate, then perform a second request that triggers early data send before verification
claims.reasoning: The PoC steps align with the code behavior: first request caches session with early data; second request reuses session, triggering cf_ngtcp2_on_session_reuse which sets use_earlydata and connected; cf_ngtcp2_send then sends request data (including Authorization header) before the new handshake completes and verification fails.

key_reasons: cf_ngtcp2_send() only checks ctx->tls_vrfy_result (pre-existing error) but not ctx->tls_handshake_complete before sending data
cf_ngtcp2_on_session_reuse() sets cf->connected=TRUE and ctx->use_earlydata=TRUE before the new handshake completes
Lines 1812-1813 explicitly track earlydata_skip when !tls_handshake_complete && use_earlydata, confirming data is sent before verification
The PoC demonstrates real exploit: Authorization header sent as early data to attacker-controlled server before certificate verification fails
This violates the security expectation that early data (0-RTT) is only safe when resuming a session with the same authenticated server
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and PoC. The code confirms that cf_ngtcp2_send() sends early data (including request headers/body) before the new TLS handshake completes and peer verification passes. The session reuse path sets cf->connected=TRUE and use_earlydata=TRUE prematurely. This allows a MITM to capture sensitive request data when the server certificate changes. We will investigate a fix requiring tls_handshake_complete before flushing early data.
